glosses: Strong in the face of fear; courageous.

examples.text: For miſerie doth braueſt mindes abate, / And make them ſeeke for that they wont to ſcorne, / Of fortune and of hope at once forlorne.

glosses: Having any sort of superiority or excellence.

examples.text:
Is it not paſſing braue to be a King,
And ride in triumph through Perſepolis?

glosses: A challenge; a defiance; bravado.

examples.text: Demetrius, thou dost overween in all; / And so in this, to bear me down with braves.

glosses: To encounter with courage and fortitude, to defy, to provoke.

glosses: To challenge (someone) or brave (a hazard or opposition).

examples.text: to defy an enemy; to defy the power of a magistrate; to defy the arguments of an opponent; to defy public opinion
I once again / Defie thee to the trial of mortal fight.

"So you actually think yours is good-looking?" sneered the Baker. "Why, I could make a better-looking one out of a piece of dough."
"I defy you to," the Hansom-driver replied. "A face like mine is not easily copied. Nor am I the only person of that opinion. All the ladies think that I am beautiful. And of course I go by what they think."

glosses: To refuse to obey.

examples.text: If you defy your teacher you may end up in detention.

British journalists shun complete respectability, feeling a duty to be ready to savage the mighty, or rummage through their bins. Elsewhere in Europe, government contracts and subsidies ensure that press barons will only defy the mighty so far.

glosses: To not conform to or follow a pattern, set of rules or expectations.

examples.text: By tossing this nineteenth electron back and forth between its own orbit and that of its lost companion more than twenty-five thousand times a second, a mutilated stone atom is able partially to defy gravity and thus successfully to ride the emerging streams of light and energy, the sunbeams, to liberty and adventure.

glosses: To renounce or dissolve all bonds of affiance, faith, or obligation with; to reject, refuse, or renounce.
